user_story: As a Plan Review Staff member, I want to Review Plans, so that I can review them for compliance and either approve, or fail or deny the plans and record any conditions, clearances, or corrections needed from the Applicant.

end

@enduml

actor Depositor

participant "PolicyValidator" as PolicyValidator
participant "Repository" as Repository

activate Depositor

activate PolicyService

deactivate PolicyService

DepositUI -> Depositor: Display disposal policy options\nand legal/collaboration guidance

activate PolicyValidator

activate PolicyService

deactivate PolicyService

alt Policy is valid
    PolicyValidator --> DepositUI: Policy approved
    deactivate PolicyValidator

    DepositUI -> Depositor: Confirm valid disposal policy
    Depositor --> DepositUI: Confirm deposit submission

    DepositUI -> Repository: Store data with disposal policy\nand compliance metadata
    activate Repository
    Repository --> DepositUI: Deposit stored successfully
    deactivate Repository

    DepositUI --> Depositor: Deposit completed with\nregistered disposal policy
else Policy is invalid or risky
    PolicyValidator --> DepositUI: Policy rejected with reasons
    deactivate PolicyValidator

    DepositUI -> Depositor: Show validation errors\nand required changes

    alt Depositor adjusts policy
        Depositor --> DepositUI: Modify disposal policy
        DepositUI -> PolicyValidator: Re-validate modified policy
        activate PolicyValidator
        PolicyValidator --> PolicyService: Request legal/collaboration rules
        activate PolicyService
        PolicyService --> PolicyValidator: Return applicable rules
        deactivate PolicyService
        ' Loop back to main validation result
        PolicyValidator --> DepositUI: Validation result
        deactivate PolicyValidator
    else Depositor cancels deposit
        Depositor --> DepositUI: Cancel deposit
        DepositUI --> Depositor: Deposit cancelled\n(no data stored)
    end
end

deactivate DepositUI
deactivate Depositor
@enduml

Here's a PlantUML sequence diagram for the user story about handling a large number of flexfields without performance impact:

```
@startuml
actor AgencyUser
database AgencyDatabase
participant "FlexFieldService" as ffs
participant "PerformanceOptimizer" as po
participant "FlexFieldCache" as fc

AgencyUser -> ffs: Submit request with many flexfields (e.g., 1000+)
ffs -> po: Check for performance bottlenecks
po --> ffs: Return performance analysis

alt Performance impact detected
    ffs -> po: Apply optimization strategy
    po --> ffs: Optimized field mapping
    ffs -> fc: Load cached flexfields
    fc --> ffs: Provide optimized flexfield set
else No performance impact
    ffs -> fc: Check cache first
    fc --> ffs: Return cached results (if available)
    ffs -> fc: Store new flexfields (asynchronously)
end

ffs -> AgencyDatabase: Persist optimized flexfields (batch operation)
AgencyDatabase --> ffs: Acknowledge persistence
ffs --> AgencyUser: Return optimized flexfield response

@enduml
```

Key elements represented:
1. Initial request from user with many flexfields
2. Performance check before processing
3. Conditional flow based on performance impact
4. Optimization strategies including caching
5. Batch persistence to avoid performance issues
6. Asynchronous operations to minimize impact

The diagram shows both the happy path and performance-aware processing, with caching playing a central role in maintaining performance.

Here's a sequence diagram for the given user story following PlantUML syntax and your requirements:

```plantuml
@startuml
actor Depositor
participant DataManagementSystem
participant PolicyValidator
participant ComplianceChecker
participant StorageSystem

Depositor -> DataManagementSystem: Initiate deposit with disposal policy specification
activate DataManagementSystem

DataManagementSystem -> Depositor: Request disposal policy details
Depositor --> DataManagementSystem: Provide disposal policy (retention period, destruction method, etc.)

DataManagementSystem -> PolicyValidator: Validate disposal policy syntax
activate PolicyValidator
PolicyValidator --> DataManagementSystem: Policy validation result (valid/invalid)
deactivate PolicyValidator

alt Policy is valid
    DataManagementSystem -> ComplianceChecker: Check against legal/collaboration requirements
    activate ComplianceChecker
    ComplianceChecker --> DataManagementSystem: Compliance status (compliant/non-compliant)
    deactivate ComplianceChecker

    alt Policy is compliant
        DataManagementSystem -> StorageSystem: Store data with disposal metadata
        StorageSystem --> DataManagementSystem: Confirm storage with disposal policy
        DataManagementSystem --> Depositor: Confirm deposit with disposal policy applied
    else Policy is non-compliant
        DataManagementSystem -> Depositor: Show compliance warnings
        Depositor --> DataManagementSystem: Modify disposal policy
        DataManagementSystem -> PolicyValidator: Revalidate modified policy
        PolicyValidator --> DataManagementSystem: Revalidation result
        if Policy still valid
            loop Until compliant
                DataManagementSystem -> ComplianceChecker: Recheck compliance
                ComplianceChecker --> DataManagementSystem: Updated compliance status
            end
            DataManagementSystem -> StorageSystem: Store data with disposal metadata
            StorageSystem --> DataManagementSystem: Confirm storage
            DataManagementSystem --> Depositor: Confirm deposit with disposal policy applied
        else
            DataManagementSystem --> Depositor: Deposit rejected (policy cannot be made compliant)
        endif
    end
else Policy is invalid
    DataManagementSystem --> Depositor: Show policy syntax errors
    Depositor --> DataManagementSystem: Correct disposal policy
    DataManagementSystem -> PolicyValidator: Revalidate corrected policy
    PolicyValidator --> DataManagementSystem: New validation result
    if Policy is valid
        loop Until compliant
            DataManagementSystem -> ComplianceChecker: Check compliance
            ComplianceChecker --> DataManagementSystem: Compliance status
        end
        DataManagementSystem -> StorageSystem: Store data with disposal metadata
        StorageSystem --> DataManagementSystem: Confirm storage
        DataManagementSystem --> Depositor: Confirm deposit with disposal policy applied
    else
        DataManagementSystem --> Depositor: Deposit rejected (invalid policy)
    endif
end

deactivate DataManagementSystem
@enduml
```

Key features of this diagram:
1. Shows the complete workflow from policy specification to storage
2. Includes validation and compliance checking
3. Handles both valid/invalid policies and compliant/non-compliant scenarios
4. Shows iterative correction loops when policies need adjustment
5. Maintains proper activation/deactivation of participants

plantuml:
It seems the user story is incomplete:  
**"As a repoadmin, I want to have Symplectic Elements to communicate"** — this lacks a clear goal or outcome. For a sequence diagram, we need to know *what* Symplectic Elements should communicate *to whom* and *for what purpose*.

Since the story is ambiguous, I will make a reasonable assumption based on common use cases in repository administration:

> **Assumed complete user story**:  
> *As a repoadmin, I want to have Symplectic Elements to communicate with the repository system to automatically deposit research outputs, so that deposits are streamlined and accurate.*

---

Based on this assumption, here is a valid PlantUML sequence diagram:

```plantuml
@startuml
actor RepoAdmin
participant SymplecticElements
participant RepositorySystem
participant DepositProcessor

RepoAdmin -> SymplecticElements: Configure integration with repository
SymplecticElements --> RepoAdmin: Integration configured

activate RepoAdmin

RepoAdmin -> SymplecticElements: Trigger deposit for a research output
SymplecticElements --> RepositorySystem: Send deposit request with metadata

activate SymplecticElements
activate RepositorySystem

RepositorySystem -> DepositProcessor: Process deposit request
DepositProcessor -> RepositorySystem: Validate metadata and permissions
RepositorySystem -> SymplecticElements: Confirm deposit success or error

alt Deposit successful
    SymplecticElements --> RepoAdmin: Deposit completed successfully
else Deposit failed
    SymplecticElements --> RepoAdmin: Deposit failed with error details
end

deactivate RepositorySystem
deactivate SymplecticElements

deactivate RepoAdmin
@enduml
```
